A bar that floats above your own keyboard. Tap it in any app, speak, and what you said is typed where your cursor is.
Dodo records only while the panel says Listening. The clip is deleted from your phone the moment it comes back as text, and it is never sent anywhere but Groq.

Dodo\'s bar is an accessibility service, which is the only way Android lets an app float above your keyboard and type into the field you are in. Android shows a broad warning for every one of these. Dodo looks at where your cursor is and nothing else, and sends audio nowhere but Groq.
Dodo transcribes with your own Groq key, so there is no account and no subscription. The free tier covers normal dictation.
Tap any text field and your keyboard comes up with Dodo\'s bar above it. Tap Start, speak, tap Done, and your words land in the field.

Dodo uses this to place its bar above your keyboard and to type what you dictate into the field you are in. It looks at where the cursor is and nothing else, keeps no record of what you type, and sends audio only to Groq with your own key.
